title: English: Grammar and Punctuation (B1)
source: Written for Kru, Nov 24 (Henry): 100 questions on grammar, punctuation and writing skills. American English.

questions.q: I ___ to Phuket three times.
questions.why: An experience up to now (three times): present perfect.

questions.q: She ___ in Chiang Mai in 2019.
questions.why: 'In 2019' is a finished time, so we use the past simple.

questions.q: Have you ___ your homework yet?
questions.why: Present perfect: have + past participle.

questions.q: I haven't seen him ___ Monday.
questions.why: 'Since' + a point in time.

questions.q: We ___ dinner already, so we're not hungry.
questions.why: 'Already' + a result now: present perfect.

questions.q: When ___ you last see her?
questions.why: 'When' asks about a finished time, so we use the past simple.

questions.q: She has worked here ___ ten years.
questions.why: 'For' + a length of time.

questions.q: Look! Somebody ___ my bike!
questions.why: We can see the result now, so we use the present perfect.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: I saw that film last night.
I have seen that film last night.
I see that film last night.
I have saw that film last night.
questions.why: With 'last night' (a finished time) we use the past simple.

questions.q: She is tired because she ___ for two hours.
questions.why: A longer activity up to now with a visible result: present perfect continuous.

questions.q: At 8 p.m. last night, I ___ TV.
questions.why: An action in progress at a time in the past: past continuous.

questions.q: They ___ football when it started to rain.
questions.why: A longer action in progress: past continuous.

questions.q: What ___ you doing at 10 o'clock?
questions.why: Past continuous question: were + you + -ing.

questions.q: I was walking home when I ___ my friend.
questions.why: The short action that interrupts uses the past simple.

questions.q: The phone rang while she ___ a shower.
questions.why: 'While' + past continuous for the longer action.

questions.q: When we arrived at the cinema, the movie ___.
questions.why: The movie started BEFORE we arrived: past perfect.

questions.q: She ___ the book before she saw the film.
questions.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

questions.q: I was tired because I ___ all night.
questions.why: Past perfect shows the earlier reason.

questions.q: By the time he called, I ___ home.
questions.why: 'By the time' + past simple: the earlier action uses past perfect.

questions.q: I ___ for an hour when the bus finally came.
questions.why: A longer action before another past action: past perfect continuous.

questions.q: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
questions.why: 'I think' + will for a prediction.

questions.q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.why: We can see the evidence now: be going to.

questions.q: We ___ my cousin on Sunday. It's arranged.
questions.why: A fixed arrangement: present continuous.

questions.q: I'm thirsty. I ___ get some water.
questions.why: A decision made at the moment of speaking: will.

questions.q: She ___ study medicine. She has already applied.
questions.why: A plan made before now: be going to.

questions.q: The train ___ at 6:15 tomorrow.
questions.why: Timetables use the present simple.

questions.q: Don't worry. I ___ help you.
questions.why: A promise or offer: will.

questions.q: This time next week I ___ on a beach.
questions.why: An action in progress at a future time: future continuous.

questions.q: I'll call you when I ___ home.
questions.why: After 'when' we use the present simple for the future.

questions.q: By 2030, scientists ___ a cure.
questions.why: 'By' + a future time: future perfect (will have + past participle).

questions.q: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.why: A general truth: zero conditional (present + present).

questions.q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
questions.why: A real possibility: first conditional (present + will).

questions.q: If I ___ rich, I would buy a boat.
questions.why: An unreal situation: second conditional (past + would). 'Were' is used for all persons.

questions.q: If you study, you ___ the test.
questions.why: First conditional: if + present, will + base verb.

questions.q: If I had more time, I ___ learn French.
questions.why: Second conditional: if + past, would + base verb.

questions.q: What would you do if you ___ a million dollars?
questions.why: Second conditional: the 'if' part uses the past simple.

questions.q: If she ___ hungry, she can eat now.
questions.why: A real situation: if + present simple.

questions.q: I won't go out ___ it stops raining.
questions.why: 'Unless' means 'if not'.

questions.q: If I were you, I ___ apologize.
questions.why: Advice with 'If I were you' uses would.

questions.q: She would be happier if she ___ more friends.
questions.why: Second conditional: the 'if' part uses the past simple.

questions.q: You ___ drive without a license.
questions.why: 'Mustn't' means it is forbidden.

questions.q: You ___ wear a uniform at my school. It's a rule.
questions.why: 'Have to' shows a rule or duty.

questions.q: ___ I open the window?
questions.why: We ask for permission with 'Can I...?'.

questions.q: I ___ speak French when I was five.
questions.why: 'Could' is the past of 'can' for ability.

questions.q: It's cold. You ___ take a coat.
questions.why: 'Should' gives advice.

questions.q: He ___ be tired. He worked all night.
questions.why: 'Must' shows that we are almost sure.

questions.q: I'm not sure, but she ___ be at the library.
questions.why: 'Might' shows a possibility.

questions.q: You ___ come to the meeting. It's not necessary.
questions.why: 'Don't have to' means it is not necessary.

questions.q: I ___ go to the dentist yesterday.
questions.why: The past of 'have to' is 'had to'.

questions.q: She ___ be at work. I saw her in the park a minute ago.
questions.why: 'Can't' shows that we are sure something is not true.

questions.q: English ___ in many countries.
questions.why: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle.

questions.q: The window ___ by a ball yesterday.
questions.why: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle.

questions.q: These cars ___ in Japan.
questions.why: Present simple passive with a plural subject: are made.

questions.q: The letter ___ last week.
questions.why: Past simple passive: was sent.

questions.q: My phone ___ at the moment.
questions.why: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

questions.q: Which sentence is the passive of 'They built the bridge in 1990'?
questions.why: was/were + past participle.

questions.q: The homework ___ yet.
questions.why: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle.

questions.q: The thief ___ by the police last night.
questions.why: Past simple passive of 'catch': was caught.

questions.q: Who ___ the Mona Lisa?
questions.why: 'Who' is the subject, so the verb is active.

questions.q: The new rules ___ to all students next week.
questions.why: Future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.q: The girl ___ is sitting there is my sister.
questions.why: 'Who' is for people.

questions.q: This is the book ___ I told you about.
questions.why: 'Which' is for things.

questions.q: That's the shop ___ I bought my shoes.
questions.why: 'Where' is for places.

questions.q: A man ___ car was stolen called the police.
questions.why: 'Whose' shows possession.

questions.q: I know a restaurant ___ serves great pizza.
questions.why: 'That' can refer to things.

questions.q: The people ___ live next door are friendly.
questions.why: 'Who' is for people.

questions.q: Bangkok, ___ is the capital of Thailand, is very big.
questions.why: Extra information between commas uses 'which', not 'that'.

questions.q: Is this the pen ___ you were looking for?
questions.why: 'That' refers to a thing.

questions.q: The teacher ___ I met yesterday is from Canada.
questions.why: 'Who' refers to a person (the object of 'met').

questions.q: The city ___ I was born is very small.
questions.why: 'In which' (or 'where') = the place of birth.

questions.q: I enjoy ___ to music.
questions.why: After 'enjoy' we use the -ing form.

questions.q: She wants ___ a doctor.
questions.why: After 'want' we use to + base verb.

questions.q: He is good at ___ chess.
questions.why: After a preposition we use the -ing form.

questions.q: We decided ___ a taxi.
questions.why: After 'decide' we use to + base verb.

questions.q: She suggested ___ to the beach.
questions.why: After 'suggest' we use the -ing form.

questions.q: I'm looking forward to ___ you.
questions.why: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so we use -ing.

questions.q: My parents let me ___ out late.
questions.why: After 'let' we use the base verb.

questions.q: He stopped ___ because he was tired.
questions.why: 'Stop + -ing' means to end an activity.

questions.q: Remember ___ the door when you leave.
questions.why: 'Remember to' = do not forget to do it.

questions.q: I'm used to ___ up early.
questions.why: 'Be used to' + -ing means something is normal for you.

questions.q: Which is a complete sentence?
questions.why: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb and makes sense by itself.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.why: In American English the comma goes inside the quotation marks.

questions.q: Which sentence has the correct end punctuation?
questions.why: An exclamation ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.q: Which is a run-on sentence?
choices: I was tired, so I went to bed.
I was tired. I went to bed.
I was tired I went to bed.
I was tired because I worked.
questions.why: Two complete sentences are joined with no punctuation or linking word.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.why: Put a comma after 'However' at the start of a sentence.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
choices: I need three things: a pen, a book, and paper.
I need: three things a pen, a book, and paper.
I need three: things a pen, a book, and paper.
I: need three things a pen, a book, and paper.
questions.why: Use a colon after a complete sentence to introduce a list.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: My brother who lives in Phuket, is a chef.
My brother, who lives in Phuket is a chef.
My brother, who lives in Phuket, is a chef.
My brother who, lives in Phuket is a chef.
questions.why: Extra information goes between two commas.

questions.q: Which is a sentence fragment?
choices: I got home when it rained.
questions.why: 'When I got home' cannot stand alone: it needs a main clause.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Although it was raining we went out.
Although it was raining, we went out.
Although, it was raining we went out.
Although it was raining. We went out.
questions.why: Put a comma after an introductory clause.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
choices: She loves reading, he prefers movies.
She loves reading; and he prefers movies.
She loves reading; he prefers movies.
She loves; reading he prefers movies.
questions.why: A semicolon joins two closely related complete sentences.

questions.q: I was very tired, ___ I finished my homework.
questions.why: 'But' shows a contrast.

questions.q: She is tall ___ her brother is short.
questions.why: 'But' joins two different ideas.

questions.q: Which word means the opposite of 'happy'?
questions.why: Sad is the opposite of happy.

questions.q: ___ the rain, we played outside.
questions.why: 'Despite' is followed by a noun.

questions.q: ___ he was tired, he kept working.
questions.why: 'Although' is followed by a clause (subject + verb).

questions.q: He didn't come ___ he was sick.
questions.why: 'Because' is followed by a clause.

questions.q: He is a very ___ person. He always helps others.
questions.why: We need an adjective before 'person'.

questions.q: Her ___ in math is amazing.
questions.why: We need a noun after 'her'.

questions.q: Read: 'Nok loves animals, but she can't have a pet because her apartment doesn't allow them. Instead, she volunteers at an animal shelter on weekends.' Why can't Nok have a pet?
questions.why: The text says her apartment doesn't allow them.

questions.q: It was late. ___, we took a taxi home.
questions.why: 'Therefore' shows a result.
